subject.title: fix(auto-reply): self-heal reply-session-init conflict instead of permanently wedging the session

question: Should maintainers accept this fenced reply-session init self-heal as the canonical fix for #101909, or require broader channel proof before merge?
rationale: The patch is source-supported and well-proven, but it intentionally changes hot session lifecycle recovery by retiring runtime state and resetting harness bindings.

options.title: Land The Fenced Self-Heal
options.body: Accept the residual session/message-delivery risk because the PR reuses existing rollover primitives, adds candidate revalidation, and includes focused plus live before/after proof.

options.title: Ask For Broader Channel Proof
options.body: Require one more Telegram or Signal live run if maintainers want channel-specific confidence before merging the runtime-level recovery.

recommendation.title: Land The Fenced Self-Heal
recommendation.body: Accept the residual session/message-delivery risk because the PR reuses existing rollover primitives, adds candidate revalidation, and includes focused plus live before/after proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh Lehman has prior history on the guarded reply-session initialization boundary this PR extends.
